info.title: API.SH: Viator
info.description: The Viator API from API.SH: public Viator data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
An attraction's tours and tickets on Viator (e.g. the Louvre), 24 a page: product code, title, description, location, category, price in USD (with discounts), rating and review count, duration, languages, coordinates and max group size. Also the attraction's name, rating and review count, image, know-before-you-go sections, description, questions and answers, and its category filters (ids to pass as `category`). Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/viator-attraction

parameters.name: attraction
parameters.description: Destination and attraction id as in viator.com/Paris-attractions/Louvre-Museum/d479-a73.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Instead of attraction: the attraction page url.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: A category id from `categories`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
A destination's (or one of its categories') tours and activities on Viator, 24 a page in the site's order: product code, title, description, from-price in USD, rating and review count, duration, flags, badges, the Travelers' Choice-style label, languages and image. Also the total count and pages, the destination's category tree (ids to pass as `category`), the popular categories with their ids, and the site's questions and answers about the destination. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/viator-destination

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description: A Viator destination id, e.g. 479 (Paris) or d479, as in viator.com/Paris/d479-ttd.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Instead of destination: a viator.com destination or category page, e.g. https://www.viator.com/Paris-tours/Walking-Tours/d479-g16-c56.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: A category id from `categories` or `category_tree` (e.g. 12046 for walking tours).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
One Viator tour or activity: title, destination, type, rating with the 1-5 star breakdown and review count, from-price in USD with any special offer, duration, free cancellation and the full cancellation policy, overview, highlights, inclusions and exclusions, additional info, languages, departure and return points, the stop-by-stop itinerary with coordinates, traveler types and group limits, supplier, tour options, photos (supplier and traveler), the 10 most relevant reviews, and the full record in `raw`.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/viator-product

get.description:
Viator's keyword search for tours, tickets and activities (24 a page, up to 200 results per query), with the site's filters and sorts: each result has its product code, title, description, destination, from-price in USD (with the before-discount price and amount saved), rating and review count, duration, free cancellation, likely-to-sell-out and private-tour flags, badges, languages, image and photo count. Also the filter options the site offers for the query. A search for a destination's name (e.g. paris) answers that destination's things to do instead (`redirected_to: destination`). Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/viator-search

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: A place, attraction or activity, e.g. eiffel tower, food tour rome.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order.

parameters.name: features
parameters.description: Comma-separated: ON_SALE, FREE_CANCELLATION, LIKELY_TO_SELL_OUT, SKIP_THE_LINE, PRIVATE_TOUR, NEW_ON_VIATOR.

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Duration ranges in minutes as min-max, comma-separated (0-60, 60-240, 240-1440, 1440-4320, 4320-).

parameters.name: min_rating
parameters.description: Minimum star rating, 1-5.

parameters.name: min_price
parameters.description: Minimum price (USD).

parameters.name: max_price
parameters.description: Maximum price (USD).

parameters.name: languages
parameters.description: Comma-separated guide languages: en, zh, nl, fr, de, it, ja, pt, ru, es.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (1-50).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
